stem.titration.bench_trace_note: Simulated response up to the current volume.
stem.titration.trace_window_note: Only the volume axis is enlarged. The vertical scale stays fixed.
stem.titration.trace_window_outside: Equivalence volume is outside this window
stem.titration.bench_signal_note: Compare the curve with the solution color. Indicator endpoint and equivalence are different signals.
stem.titration.invest_collection_empty: Save a colorless observation and a pink observation to compare.
stem.titration.invest_collection_before: Save a colorless observation at an earlier volume.
stem.titration.invest_collection_after: Save a pink observation at a later volume.
stem.titration.invest_collection_mismatc: Use observations from the same setup and indicator, with the pink reading at a higher volume.
stem.titration.invest_collection_narrow: Both sides are saved. Collect observations closer together to narrow the gap.
stem.titration.invest_collection_ready: Your saved observations bracket the color change within 0.2 mL.
stem.titration.invest_collection_target: Target: two saved observations no more than 0.2 mL apart.
stem.titration.invest_collection_saved: This tracker uses saved investigation readings. Moving the live flask does not save an observation.
stem.titration.invest_report_sample: Starting sample: 25.0 mL of 0.1 M HCl
stem.titration.invest_report_ungraded: Ready for review. Completion is not an automatic grade.
stem.titration.invest_report_scope: This report includes the starting reading and reviewed color-change pair. Other notebook entries are not included.
stem.titration.invest_resolution: The simulation advances in 0.1 mL steps, which can skip the indicator transition range. Report an interval rather than an exact endpoint.
stem.titration.invest_report_snapshot: Saved investigation: later bench changes do not alter this downloaded copy.
stem.titration.invest_map_below: {label}: {volume} mL is below the shown range.
stem.titration.invest_map_above: {label}: {volume} mL is above the shown range.
stem.titration.invest_map_evidence: The circle and square mark the two saved readings. The shaded span shows their volume gap, not an exact endpoint.
stem.titration.invest_map_controls: Zoom changes only this diagram. The experiment and saved readings stay unchanged.
stem.titration.invest_report_help: Download an HTML copy with the close-up diagram to keep or share. Open it in a browser to print or save as PDF.
stem.titration.invest_hint_predict: The flask starts with 25.0 mL of 0.1 M HCl. The NaOH is also 0.1 M. Think about the 1:1 reaction and how much base would react with the acid.
stem.titration.invest_hint_baseline: Save a reading at 0.0 mL before adding NaOH. The numerical volume and pH will be copied into your notebook.
stem.titration.invest_hint_collect: Use larger additions at first. Near 25 mL, save readings after 0.1 mL additions. Find a colorless reading followed by a pink reading no more than 0.2 mL apart.
stem.titration.invest_hint_compare: The open circle and diamond are saved observations. The dashed guides show their differences; they do not predict the curve between the points.
stem.titration.invest_hint_explain: Use both saved volumes and their pH values. Explain why a color-change signal and the amount required by the reaction are different ideas.
stem.titration.invest_prediction_prompt: At about what added volume do you predict the flask will first show a color change?
stem.titration.invest_prediction_help: Enter 0.0–50.0 mL in 0.1 mL steps. This is a prediction, not a graded answer.
stem.titration.invest_prediction_zero: Return to 0.0 mL to save your prediction before collecting readings.
stem.titration.invest_baseline_prompt: Save the 0.0 mL reading so you can compare the starting flask with later observations.
stem.titration.invest_collect_prompt: Add NaOH and save observations. Find the last colorless reading and the first pink reading within a 0.2 mL interval.
stem.titration.invest_collection_unsaved: The current flask reading has not been saved to this investigation.
stem.titration.invest_already_saved: This observation is already part of your investigation. Add titrant to collect another.
stem.titration.invest_revisit_note: Revisiting moves the simulation back near the color change. Your saved notebook observations stay in place.
stem.titration.invest_compare_prompt: Compare the two saved observations below. Notice how much the pH changes over a small added volume.
stem.titration.invest_explain_prompt: What does your color-change interval tell you? Use your volumes and pH readings, compare with your prediction, and explain why an indicator endpoint and equivalence are different signals.
stem.titration.invest_explanation_help: Saved as you type. Up to 700 characters. Your explanation is saved for review and is not automatically graded.
stem.titration.invest_complete_note: Your prediction, saved-reading evidence, and explanation are ready to review. This completion records your work; it does not grade your explanation.
stem.titration.invest_distinction: Equivalence is the amount required by the reaction stoichiometry. The indicator endpoint is a color-change signal. Your readings bracket that signal at this simulation’s volume resolution.
stem.titration.invest_intro: Predict, collect a color-change interval, and explain it using your saved readings. HCl + NaOH with phenolphthalein.
stem.titration.invest_start_note: Starting a new investigation sets this setup to 0.0 mL and clears the guide answers. Your notebook readings are kept.
stem.titration.invest_room: Make room for at least three readings in the notebook before starting. Remove individual readings or download your notebook before clearing it.
stem.titration.invest_paused: Guidance is paused for this setup. This investigation uses HCl + NaOH with phenolphthalein. Your guide answers and saved evidence are kept.
stem.titration.invest_restore_note: Restoring the investigation setup returns its volume to 0.0 mL.
stem.titration.invest_full: The notebook is full. Remove unneeded readings to make room. Removing investigation evidence updates your progress; Undo removal restores it.
stem.titration.comparison_scale_note: Axes zoom to the two saved readings. Dashed guides show the volume and response differences.
stem.titration.comparison_same_volume: Choose different volumes to calculate an average change.
stem.titration.comparison_average_note: Calculated from the rounded readings saved in the notebook.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_intro: Explore the observations you saved, one titration setup at a time.
stem.titration.notebook_zoom_help: Close-up follows the selected reading and includes saved points within 0.5 mL on either side. The reading list always includes every reading in this setup.
stem.titration.notebook_zoom_full_help: Axes fit all saved readings in this setup. Use the close-up to separate nearby volumes.
stem.titration.notebook_zoom_count: Showing {visible} of {total} readings in this setup.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_points: Points show saved readings; no curve is fitted.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_unavailable: These saved values cannot be plotted. Use the reading list to inspect them.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_help: Select a point or use the reading list. Overlapping points remain individually selectable in the list.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_note_help: Changes save as you type and are included in the notebook and CSV. Press Escape to finish editing.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_empty_note: Record what you notice in this saved reading.
stem.titration.notebook_plot_note: Selecting readings or changing the scale does not change the experiment. Observation edits update the saved notebook.
stem.titration.notebook_restored: Readings, notes, and investigation evidence restored.
stem.titration.bench_dose_help: Use 0.1 mL increments. Remaining simulation range:
stem.titration.bench_dose_invalid: Enter a positive volume within the remaining range, in 0.1 mL steps.
stem.titration.bench_compare_help: Save and choose two different readings from the same titration setup and signal type.
stem.titration.notebook_spaces: {count} spaces available. Remove individual readings to make room.
stem.titration.bench_notebook_help: Save displayed simulation readings to compare later. Readings stay in the notebook when you change setups; up to 40 can be kept.
stem.titration.notebook_undo_help: Restore the most recent removal or clear, including saved notes and investigation evidence. Available until your next notebook or investigation edit.
stem.titration.notebook_evidence_help: Marked readings belong to your investigation. Removing evidence updates its progress and report. Undo removal restores it.
stem.titration.bench_notes_help: Add your observations below each saved reading. Notes save as you type and are included in the CSV download.
stem.titration.notebook_view_help: Filters change the reading list. Comparison, plots, CSV, and Clear notebook use all saved readings.
stem.titration.notebook_view_current_hel: Matches the current titration setup, signal type, and indicator.
stem.titration.notebook_view_evidence_he: Shows readings captured by your current investigation, including when it is paused.
stem.titration.notebook_view_first: Save a reading to begin your notebook.
stem.titration.notebook_view_empty: No saved readings match this view. Your other readings are still in the notebook.
stem.titration.dilution_visual_intro: Compare the measured stock aliquot on the left with the final solution on the right. Adjust the calculator above to update the view.
stem.titration.dilution_fallback: 3D is unavailable. The 2D comparison and calculator remain available.
stem.titration.dilution_solute_constant: Same amount of solute in both views:
stem.titration.dilution_visual_note: Gold markers represent equal portions of solute, not individual atoms. Their size changes to fit shallow liquid; compare their count. Vessel dimensions and colors are illustrative. Use the numerical readings and the preparation procedure below. Mouse drag or arrow keys rotate; +/− zoom; 0 resets. Touch swipes scroll the page.
stem.titration.measure_parts_scale: Each horizontal bar follows the readings from 0.0 to 50.0 mL. Only the shaded section counts toward this delivery.
stem.titration.measure_parts_refill: Refill: the scale returns to 0.0 mL.
stem.titration.measure_parts_zero: No volume has been counted since this start reading.
stem.titration.measure_help: Set a start reading, then add titrant to measure the volume delivered since that mark.
stem.titration.measure_scale_note: Each scale shows one 50 mL fill. Read the numbered values; use the reading lens for the meniscus close-up.
stem.titration.measure_empty: Choose Set start reading to begin.
stem.titration.measure_refill_note: A refill returns the burette scale to the top. Delivered volume continues to accumulate.
stem.titration.measure_mark_note: Setting or clearing a start mark does not add titrant or save a notebook reading. The mark is cleared if the setup changes or the volume moves below it.
stem.titration.lens_empty: The burette is empty at 50.0 mL.
stem.titration.lens_dark: Dark titrant: the guide follows the upper visible edge.
stem.titration.lens_clear: Clear titrant: the guide follows the bottom of the meniscus.
stem.titration.lens_fill_note: This is the current burette fill reading. Total delivered volume also includes earlier fills.
stem.titration.color_explorer_help: Preview only: no titrant is added and no readings are saved.
stem.titration.color_explorer_note: Compare the samples on white. The live sample follows your experiment; the reference stays at the value you choose.
stem.titration.color_redox_note: Self-indicating permanganate. Compare the color with the potential curve and added volume.
stem.titration.color_indicator_note: Compare the color with the pH curve. A color change alone does not locate the equivalence point.
stem.titration.color_white_note: Simulated colors shown on white; glass and lighting can change their appearance.
stem.titration.nav_apparatus_hint: Follow additions and the live curve.
stem.titration.nav_flask_hint: Inspect the solution and compare colors.
stem.titration.nav_burette_hint: Read the scale and track delivered volume.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_empty: Load a recorded sample to inspect how its solid mass moves between the boat and receiver.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_boat_rea: The boat holds the starting solid. The residue setting takes effect when you pour.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_boat_wet: The model rinse has moved the remaining solid into the receiver. This boat is wet; its mass cannot be used as a dry after-transfer reading.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_boat_res: The highlighted grains represent residue still in the boat. Use the dry mass difference or rinse and update the transfer record.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_boat_emp: No solid remains in the boat at this model setting. The entire sample reached the receiver.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_receiver: The receiver is empty. Pour the sample to see the delivered solid.
The receiver holds all of the starting solid after the model rinse. The blue liquid is rinse solvent and is excluded from the solid-mass totals.
These grains represent the delivered solid. The mass cards and bar show the measured split; the grain count is schematic.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_bench_no: Inspect either vessel, or follow the sample automatically. View changes preserve the current trial and its record.
stem.titration.inspect_filler_note: The filler stays above the pipette. Use it to draw solution; keep liquid out of the filler and keep the pipette vertical.
stem.titration.inspect_receiver_blown: Extra liquid has entered the receiver. Its volume is not modeled, so this delivery cannot use the nominal 25 mL result.
stem.titration.inspect_receiver_done: The receiver now holds the calibrated delivery. The highlighted tip still contains retained liquid; leave it in this non-blow-out pipette.
stem.titration.inspect_receiver_wall: The highlighted tip is against the receiver wall. Allow gravity drainage and the pipette’s specified wait before withdrawing it along the wall.
stem.titration.inspect_receiver_ready: The meniscus is set. Move the vertical pipette so its tip touches the receiver’s inside wall before draining.
stem.titration.inspect_receiver_empty: The aliquot receiver is still empty. Condition, fill, and set the pipette before moving to this vessel.
stem.titration.inspect_tip_blown: The retained liquid has been forced out. Restart pipetting to obtain a new calibrated delivery.
stem.titration.inspect_tip_done: This enlarged tip shows the retained liquid included in the pipette’s delivery calibration. Do not subtract it from 25 mL or force it out.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_set: The lower meniscus meets the calibration mark. Keep the pipette vertical for delivery.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_level: Your eye is level with the mark. The meniscus is still above it; release excess solution to the waste receiver until the lower meniscus meets the mark.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_above: The meniscus is above the mark and the eye is too high. Align your eye before setting the lower meniscus.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_empty: This close-up shows the calibration mark. Load a prepared solution, condition the pipette, and fill it before setting the meniscus.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_conditioned: The pipette is conditioned and ready to fill. Use the filler to draw solution above the calibration mark.
stem.titration.inspect_mark_ready: The solution is loaded. Condition the pipette with it before filling above the calibration mark.
stem.titration.inspect_bench_note: Choose a close-up to inspect the apparatus, or follow the current step automatically. Changing the view keeps your practice record.
stem.titration.equip_balance_desc: Separate container mass from sample mass.
stem.titration.equip_balance_technique: Check that the balance is level, ready, and zeroed according to its instructions before starting.
stem.titration.equip_balance_text1: Use a clean, suitable weighing vessel for powders. Place it centrally on the pan.
stem.titration.equip_balance_text2: Close the draft shield and wait for stability, then tare the empty vessel. Tare subtracts its mass from the reading.
stem.titration.equip_balance_text3: Add sample carefully, close the shield, and wait for a stable reading. Record the actual mass with its unit.
stem.titration.equip_balance_error: Reading before stability, spilling powder on the pan, or taring away some of the sample.
stem.titration.equip_balance_safety: Use the approved weighing method and clean up spills according to the lab procedure.
stem.titration.equip_boat_desc: Contain a solid and account for its transfer.
stem.titration.equip_boat_technique: Choose a clean, dry vessel compatible with the solid and any solvent used to rinse it.
stem.titration.equip_boat_text1: Use the boat to keep solid off the balance pan. Measure sample mass separately from the container mass.
stem.titration.equip_boat_text2: Guide the solid into the receiving vessel without spilling. Some material may remain on the boat.
stem.titration.equip_boat_text3: Follow the method: rinse compatible residue into the receiver, or determine the transferred mass by weighing before and after transfer.
stem.titration.equip_boat_error: Assuming all weighed solid reached the solution when some remains in the boat.
stem.titration.equip_boat_safety: Some solvents attack plastic boats. Check compatibility before rinsing.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_technique: Use a clean, dry, compatible spatula and the portioning method specified for the reagent.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_text1: Choose a suitable clean tool before taking a working portion of solid.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_text2: Use smaller portions as you approach the target. A scoop does not have a fixed mass; check the balance reading.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_text3: Do not return excess material to the stock container. Handle leftovers and clean the tool as directed.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_error: Cross-contaminating stock or treating scoop size as a calibrated measurement.
stem.titration.equip_spatula_safety: Avoid raising dust; follow the handling controls for the actual solid.
stem.titration.prep_weigh_hint: Practice tare, fine additions, and a stable reading.
stem.titration.prep_transfer_hint: Account for the material left in the boat.
stem.titration.prep_volume_hint: Dissolve, transfer rinsings, make to volume, and mix.
stem.titration.aliquot_path_hint: Deliver a measured portion with a volumetric pipette.
stem.titration.path_weigh_changed: Sample changed after weighing. Update its record.
stem.titration.path_transfer_changed: Rinsed after recording. Update the delivered mass.
stem.titration.path_overshoot: Above the mark. Restart this preparation.
stem.titration.path_blowout: Tip liquid forced out. Restart pipetting.
stem.titration.path_all_recorded: Every activity has a current record. Choose a stage to review it.
stem.titration.path_copies: Each activity keeps its own sample copy. Changing an earlier activity does not replace later records. You can open any stage to review or restart it.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_empty: The pan is empty and no tare offset is stored. Gross and net are both zero.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_untared: The empty boat is on the pan. Its mass is included in the display until you tare it.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_removed: The pan is empty, but the stored tare is still subtracted. This is a negative display offset, not a negative sample mass. Returning the boat restores its load on the pan.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_tared: The boat still has mass after taring. Subtracting its stored mass makes the net display zero.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_sample: Gross mass includes the boat and its sample. Subtracting the stored boat mass leaves the current sample mass on the net display.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_scale: All bars use the same fixed mass scale. Left of zero is negative; right of zero is positive.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_off_pan: Sample retained in the boat off the pan
stem.titration.weigh_explain_open: The shield is open. These model values explain the display; close the shield before recording.
stem.titration.weigh_explain_current: This breakdown follows the current pan load. A saved mass changes only when you record again or restart the practice.
stem.titration.weigh_target_off_low: Sample is below this close-up range. Its arrow sits at the left edge.
stem.titration.weigh_target_off_high: Sample is above this close-up range. Its arrow sits at the right edge.
stem.titration.weigh_target_legend: Shaded band: 0.4980–0.5020 g. The line marks the 0.5000 g target. The circle or arrow marks the sample. This practice band is not measurement uncertainty.
stem.titration.weigh_target_off_pan: This guide follows the sample retained in the boat, even when the boat is off the pan.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_boat: Place or return the boat to compare additions.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_tare: Tare the empty boat before comparing additions.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_shield: Open the draft shield to compare additions.
stem.titration.weigh_additions: Spatula additions · use smaller portions near the target
stem.titration.weigh_compare_intro: Compare the sample mass after one addition. Only the + buttons add material. Predictions use fixed practice portions; real scoops vary.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_within: Would land within the target band.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_below: Would stay below the target band.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_above: Would be above the target band.
stem.titration.weigh_compare_limit: This portion would exceed the 2.0000 g practice limit.
stem.titration.weigh_next_open: Open the draft shield to place the boat.
stem.titration.weigh_next_boat: Place the boat on the pan.
stem.titration.weigh_next_tare: Tare the empty boat to exclude its mass.
stem.titration.weigh_next_close_tare: Close the shield before taring the empty boat.
stem.titration.weigh_next_open_add: Open the shield to add sample with the spatula.
stem.titration.weigh_next_add: Add a coarse portion, then use smaller additions near the target.
stem.titration.weigh_next_close: Close the shield before recording a mass.
stem.titration.weigh_next_transfer: Mass recorded. Study how to transfer the sample without losing material.
stem.titration.weigh_next_record: Record the stable sample mass, even if it differs from the target.
stem.titration.weigh_goal: Aim for 0.5000 g. The practice target band is ±0.0020 g; it is not the balance uncertainty.
stem.titration.weigh_equation: Net = gross − tare. Removing a tared boat leaves a negative reading.
stem.titration.weigh_transfer_hint: Next, check how much of this sample reaches the receiver.
stem.titration.weigh_record_stale: Sample changed. Close the shield and record the new mass.
stem.titration.weigh_model_note: Practice model: fixed additions, a 2 g sample limit, and immediate stability with the shield closed. Real scoops vary; wait for the instrument stability indicator. Four decimals show display resolution, not guaranteed accuracy.
stem.titration.weigh_scope: Progress stays while you browse equipment. Restart clears this practice record. This exercise does not change the live titration or its notebook.
stem.titration.transfer_inspect_balance_: Bar widths show the current solid masses. Grain drawings are schematic; rinse liquid is excluded.
stem.titration.transfer_cancel_note: Subtract the same empty-boat mass from both readings. Their difference stays the same.
stem.titration.transfer_cancel_scale: Every bar uses 0.0000–5.0000 g in both views.
stem.titration.transfer_cancel_removed: The boat contribution is removed from both readings. The delivered solid is unchanged.
stem.titration.transfer_cancel_included: The matching hatched sections show the same boat mass in both dry readings.
stem.titration.transfer_cancel_scope: Diagram only: this does not tare the balance or change the transfer.
stem.titration.transfer_next_dry_recorde: Dry transfer recorded. Continue with this delivered mass, or rinse the residue and record the updated result.
stem.titration.transfer_next_recorded: Transfer recorded. Continue to solution preparation with the delivered mass.
stem.titration.transfer_next_load: Load a current recorded mass from the weighing activity to begin.
stem.titration.transfer_next_pour: Choose a model residue setting, then pour the solid into the receiver.
stem.titration.transfer_next_compare: Compare the dry masses to find how much arrived. Record this result, or rinse the remaining solid into the receiver.
stem.titration.transfer_next_finish: All of the model sample is in the receiver. Record the transfer before continuing to solution preparation.
stem.titration.transfer_intro: Explore how residue changes the mass delivered to a receiver. The exercise keeps a copy of your recorded sample.
stem.titration.transfer_no_record: No current weighing record. Record the sample mass on the balance first.
stem.titration.transfer_reload_note: Loading a sample starts a new transfer; navigating between guides keeps this trial.
stem.titration.transfer_source_changed: The weighing record has changed or is unavailable. This trial still uses its original sample
stem.titration.transfer_residue_setting: Residue left by a dry pour (model setting)
stem.titration.transfer_setting_hint: Choose 0–10% before pouring. This is an example setting, not a prediction for a real powder.
stem.titration.transfer_setting_locked: Restart the transfer to compare a different residue setting.
stem.titration.transfer_difference_note: These are model dry masses. The same boat mass cancels, leaving the mass delivered.
stem.titration.transfer_wet_warning: The boat is now wet. Do not use its wet mass as the dry after-transfer measurement; rinse liquid would change that reading.
stem.titration.transfer_method_rinse: Method: complete rinse in this model
stem.titration.transfer_record_stale: The received mass changed after rinsing. Record the transfer again to update this result.
stem.titration.transfer_model_note: Illustrative model: no spills, masses rounded to 0.0001 g, and a complete rinse in one action. In a real procedure, use compatible solvent and rinse as directed; one rinse is not a guarantee of complete transfer.
stem.titration.transfer_preparation_note: Dissolve the solid and transfer it with its rinsings before making up the final solution volume. This exercise does not change the live titration or its notebook.
stem.titration.transfer_use_delivered: Use the mass that reached the receiver when calculating concentration. It can differ from the original weighed mass.
stem.titration.transfer_update_before_pr: The transfer changed after recording. Update its record before using a mass for solution preparation.
stem.titration.prep_preview_intro: Choose an addition to see its dashed meniscus. Only Apply changes the flask volume.
stem.titration.prep_preview_warning: This addition would overshoot. Applying it will require restarting this preparation.
stem.titration.prep_preview_blocked: The flask is already above the mark. Restart before trying another addition.
stem.titration.prep_preview_note: Model volumes are teaching aids. The close-up exaggerates distance from the mark; real drop sizes vary.
stem.titration.predict_study: Use the diagrams and calculation to compare solute mass and concentration. You can try a prediction whenever you are ready.
stem.titration.predict_prompt: Compared with the recorded 100 mL solution, will each quantity be lower, the same, or higher in your selected example? Choose both, then check.
stem.titration.predict_optional: Optional practice: you can reveal the comparison without answering. Predictions are not saved or graded.
stem.titration.compare_intro: Each example starts from your recorded, mixed 100 mL solution. These comparisons do not use up solution or change your preparation or pipetting records.
stem.titration.compare_diagram_note: Each tile represents 25 mL of solution. Dots compare solute amounts within this example; they are not visible grains or molecule counts. These are abstract volume diagrams, not vessels.
stem.titration.compare_aliquot_note: One quarter of the volume carries one quarter of the solute mass. A representative portion of a mixed solution has the same concentration.
stem.titration.compare_dilution_note: The whole sample keeps its solute mass in a larger final solution volume. Its mass concentration decreases.
stem.titration.compare_method: The selected volume is the final solution volume, not the amount of solvent to add. In practice, use suitable larger volumetric glassware, transfer quantitatively, make to its mark, and mix. Do not overfill the 100 mL flask.
stem.titration.compare_model: Calculated examples assume no loss or reaction and complete mixing. They use mass concentration in g/L, not molarity.
stem.titration.preparation_next_load: Use a current transfer record to begin preparing a solution.
stem.titration.preparation_next_dissolve: Dissolve the delivered sample in a suitable portion of solvent before making up the final volume.
stem.titration.preparation_next_transfer: Transfer the solution and all receiver and funnel rinsings into the volumetric flask. Keep below the mark.
stem.titration.preparation_next_over: The meniscus is above the mark. Restart this practice preparation; removing mixed solution does not restore the intended concentration.
stem.titration.preparation_next_done: Preparation recorded. Use the delivered mass and final solution volume to calculate mass concentration.
stem.titration.preparation_next_eye: Align your eye with the mark, then bring the bottom of the clear meniscus to it.
stem.titration.preparation_next_mix: The bottom of the meniscus meets the mark. Stopper securely and mix by repeated inversion.
stem.titration.preparation_next_fill: Add solvent carefully. Switch to the smaller model additions near the mark.
stem.titration.preparation_intro: Practice the order of preparation and learn why the final solution volume matters. This trial keeps a copy of your delivered sample mass.
stem.titration.preparation_no_source: A current recorded transfer is needed to load a sample.
stem.titration.preparation_reload_note: Loading again starts a new preparation. Navigating between equipment keeps this trial.
stem.titration.preparation_source_change: The transfer record has changed or is unavailable. This preparation still uses its original delivered mass.
stem.titration.preparation_empty: Load a delivered sample to begin
stem.titration.prep_preview_legend: Solid meniscus: current level. Dashed meniscus: preview after the addition.
stem.titration.preparation_volume_note: The close-up exaggerates small differences from the mark. The extra volume readout is a teaching aid; a real flask has one calibration mark, not a graduated scale.
stem.titration.preparation_above: Above the mark — preparation needs restarting.
stem.titration.preparation_at: At the mark — stop adding solvent.
stem.titration.preparation_below: Below the mark — more solvent is needed.
stem.titration.preparation_mass_not_mola: This is mass per solution volume. Molar concentration also requires the solute’s molar mass.
stem.titration.preparation_model_note: Illustrative model: the sample dissolves completely, transfer with rinsings is complete, and the flask starts at 95.00 mL. Fixed additions, liquid heights, and mixing in one action are simplified. Real drop sizes, solubility, temperature, and mixing requirements depend on the procedure.
stem.titration.preparation_method_note: Follow the reviewed procedure and the flask’s calibration temperature. Make up to the final solution volume, not by adding 100 mL of solvent. These practice results do not change the live titration.
stem.titration.aliquot_equip_desc: Transfer one calibrated volume of solution.
stem.titration.aliquot_equip_technique: This exercise uses a 25 mL non-blow-out volumetric pipette. Condition it with the solution, fill above the mark with a filler, set the meniscus at eye level, and deliver vertically against the receiving wall. Follow the specified drain and waiting times; leave retained tip liquid in place.
stem.titration.aliquot_equip_error1: Skipping solution conditioning or setting the meniscus from the wrong viewing height.
stem.titration.aliquot_equip_error2: Forcing retained liquid out of this non-blow-out pipette or ignoring its drain instructions.
stem.titration.aliquot_equip_safety: Never mouth pipette. Use a compatible filler and support the glass near its top when fitting it. Other pipette types have different delivery instructions; check their markings.
stem.titration.aliquot_mark_detail: Set the lower meniscus at the mark
stem.titration.aliquot_next_load: Finish and mix a preparation, then load its solution to begin.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_condition: Condition a clean pipette with a small working portion of the solution. Collect the rinse as waste; do not return it to the stock.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_fill: Use the fitted pipette filler to draw solution above the mark. Keep liquid out of the filler.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_eye: Keep the pipette vertical and bring your eye level with its calibration mark.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_adjust: Release excess solution to a suitable waste receiver until the bottom of the meniscus meets the mark.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_wall: Move to the receiving vessel. Keep the pipette vertical and place its tip against the inside wall.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_drain: Allow gravity drainage and follow the pipette’s specified waiting time before withdrawing the tip along the wall.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_blown: Forcing out the retained liquid adds more than the calibrated delivery. The actual extra volume is not modeled, so the 25 mL result is no longer valid.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_recorded: Aliquot recorded. Taking a well-mixed portion changes the amount of solute, while its concentration stays the same.
stem.titration.aliquot_next_record: The calibrated delivery is complete. Leave the retained tip liquid in this non-blow-out pipette and record the aliquot.
stem.titration.aliquot_phase_delivered: 5 · Leave the tip liquid and record
stem.titration.aliquot_intro: Practise with a standard non-blow-out volumetric pipette calibrated to deliver 25 mL. An aliquot is a measured portion of a well-mixed solution.
stem.titration.aliquot_no_source: A completed, mixed preparation is needed.
stem.titration.aliquot_snapshot_note: This exercise uses a copy of the prepared solution. Loading again starts a new pipetting trial.
stem.titration.aliquot_source_changed: The preparation has changed or is unavailable. This trial keeps its original concentration until you load again.
stem.titration.aliquot_empty: Load a prepared solution to begin
stem.titration.aliquot_blown_note: Extra liquid was forced into the receiver. Do not use the nominal 25 mL value for this delivery.
stem.titration.aliquot_retained_note: The retained liquid is already accounted for in this pipette’s delivery calibration. Do not subtract it from 25 mL or force it out.
stem.titration.aliquot_record_invalid: Your earlier record is no longer valid after blowing out the tip. Restart to record a new aliquot.
stem.titration.aliquot_same_c: Same concentration as the prepared solution
stem.titration.aliquot_mistake_hint: Explore a technique error: see what happens if the retained liquid is forced out.
stem.titration.aliquot_model_note: Illustrative model: conditioning, drainage, and the specified wait each finish in one action. Working-solution use, rinse waste, and retained-liquid volumes are not tracked. Vessel shapes and liquid levels are schematic. The prepared solution and live titration are unchanged.
stem.titration.equip_flask_desc: Prepare a solution to one calibrated volume.
stem.titration.equip_flask_technique: A volumetric flask is calibrated to contain its marked volume, not to deliver that volume when poured.
stem.titration.equip_flask_text1: Transfer the dissolved solute and its rinsings into the flask. Keep the liquid below the calibration mark.
stem.titration.equip_flask_text2: At the specified temperature, add solvent dropwise. View the bottom of the clear meniscus at eye level against the single mark.
stem.titration.equip_flask_text3: Stopper securely and invert repeatedly to mix the entire solution before taking an aliquot.
stem.titration.equip_flask_error: Overshooting the mark changes the concentration; removing some mixed solution does not correct it.
stem.titration.equip_flask_safety: Follow the reviewed preparation procedure; a volumetric flask is not a heating vessel.
stem.titration.equip_filler_technique: Use a compatible filler and follow its controls; bulb and lever designs differ.
stem.titration.equip_filler_text1: Support the pipette near its top when fitting the filler. Do not force glass into a tight adapter.
stem.titration.equip_filler_text2: Draw solution above the mark, then adjust the meniscus to it. Keep liquid out of the filler.
stem.titration.equip_filler_text3: Let a standard volumetric pipette drain by gravity against the receiving wall. Follow its drain time; do not blow out its retained tip liquid.
stem.titration.equip_filler_error: Drawing liquid into the bulb or forcing the final liquid out.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_desc: Fill the burette, then remove the funnel.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_technique: A funnel is a filling aid; it does not stay in place during a measured titration.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_text1: Secure the burette, close its stopcock, and place a waste beaker underneath.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_text2: Allow air to escape around the funnel stem. Watch the burette level and avoid overfilling.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_text3: Remove the funnel before taking the initial reading. Later drips would change the volume after that reading.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_error: Leaving the funnel in the burette during titration.
stem.titration.equip_funnel_safety: Fill at a safe working height.
stem.titration.equip_stand_desc: Support the burette above the receiving flask.
stem.titration.equip_stand_technique: Set up a stable support before filling the burette.
stem.titration.equip_stand_text1: Place the stand on a level bench, away from its edge.
stem.titration.equip_stand_text2: Use a suitable burette clamp. Support the glass while adjusting the grip; do not overtighten.
stem.titration.equip_stand_text3: Keep the burette vertical, with its tip above the flask opening and room to swirl.
stem.titration.equip_stand_error: Loose grips, unstable bases, or a burette leaning sideways.
stem.titration.equip_stand_safety: Check the support before adding reagent.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_desc: Mix evenly with a magnetic stir bar.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_technique: Gentle mixing distributes each addition through the analyte. A deep vortex is not the goal.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_text1: With stirring off, place a clean stir bar in the flask and center it on the plate.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_text2: Increase stirring gradually until the solution mixes without splashing. Keep any probe clear of the moving bar.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_text3: Switch stirring off before moving the vessel or recovering the bar. Handle the solution as directed by the lab procedure.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_error: Excessive speed can cause splashing or make the stir bar lose its smooth rotation.
stem.titration.equip_stirrer_safety: On a combined hotplate and stirrer, heating is a separate control. Leave it off unless the procedure requires it.
stem.titration.equip_probe_desc: Measure acidity and follow a potentiometric endpoint.
stem.titration.equip_probe_technique: Use the instructions for the actual electrode and meter. This illustration does not calibrate the simulated pH signal.
stem.titration.equip_probe_text1: Calibrate with fresh buffer portions spanning the expected pH range. Rinse between buffers; never return used buffer to its bottle.
stem.titration.equip_probe_text2: Immerse the sensing region as specified. Keep the tip clear of the vessel and stir bar, then wait for a stable reading.
stem.titration.equip_probe_text3: Rinse with deionized water and store in the manufacturer-specified solution. Do not use deionized water for long-term storage of this glass pH electrode.
stem.titration.equip_probe_error: Using the electrode to stir, contaminating calibration buffers, or letting the glass bulb dry out.
stem.titration.equip_probe_safety: The sensing bulb is fragile. Secure the electrode before starting a stirrer.
stem.titration.equip_illustration_note: Illustrated guide. Selecting a step does not operate equipment or change your experiment. Follow your reviewed lab procedure and equipment instructions.
stem.titration.equip_source: Read the technique reference (opens a new tab)
stem.titration.nav_aids_hint: Each aid opens its matching close-up.
stem.titration.inspector_help: Step through an illustrative mixing cue for the current setup. No titrant is added and recorded readings stay unchanged. The timeline is illustrative, not a measurement of reaction speed.
stem.titration.bench_loading: Loading the 3D bench. The diagram remains available below.
stem.titration.bench_flask_guide: Watch the liquid surface rise and compare the solution color with the indicator status. The white tile helps the color stand out.
stem.titration.bench_burette_guide: Track the meniscus as you add titrant. The burette readout describes the current fill; cumulative titrant volume also includes previous fills.
stem.titration.bench_full_guide: Follow an addition from the burette tip into the flask. Use the close-ups to inspect each vessel, then compare the readings with the curve below.
stem.titration.bench_scale_note: Illustrative apparatus: dimensions, liquid heights, and drop animation are not a calibrated measurement scale. Use the numerical readings. Drag with a mouse or use the camera buttons; touch swipes scroll the page.
stem.titration.animated_reference_curve_: Animated reference curve showing pH versus titrant volume for a strong acid titrated by a strong base.
